transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I hope I'm doing this right, I've never really done this before. 

I'm here because... well, things have been really overwhelming with my house. Everyone keeps acting like this foreclosure is just, you know, regular paperwork and a few missed payments. And I really don't want to sound difficult or unreasonable—I know how it must sound to someone on the outside—but I just know that the bank, the loan servicer, and honestly even some people at my job have been quietly working together to push me out of my house. 

I mean, they keep showing me all these documents, but no amount of papers they show me changes what I’ve been seeing happening for almost two years now. Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm explaining things clearly for you, I don't want to come across the wrong way.
When you think about the bank and your job working together against you, is there any part of you that wonders whether you might be mistaken about this, or are you completely certain it's happening?

I... I really wish I could say I was mistaken. I know it would be so much easier for everyone if I was just confused about the paperwork, and I hate being the kind of person who, you know, makes a fuss or seems paranoid. I really do. 

But... no, I'm completely certain. I've been watching this happen for almost two years now. I know the bank and the loan servicer and the people at work are coordinating this. It’s just... the things I’ve seen, the way they talk to me, the timing of everything—it all lines up too perfectly to be an accident. They keep putting these foreclosure documents in front of me, trying to make it look like it's just about missed payments, but I know what's really going on underneath it all. No matter what papers they try to show me, it doesn't change the reality of what they're doing. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound crazy or stubborn to you. I just... I have to trust what I've been seeing with my own eyes, right? Is it okay that I'm being this honest with you about it?

Besides what you've observed with documents and the way people talk to you, have you ever heard voices, seen things, or experienced anything through your senses that other people around you couldn't perceive or didn't seem to notice?

No, no, I've never had anything like that. I mean, I don't hear voices or see things that aren't there or anything... I know some people deal with that, and I have so much sympathy for them, but that's not what this is. 

I just notice the things that are actually happening, you know? Like the way my manager looks at me when I come in, or the specific wording they use in the emails from the bank. It's all real things that anyone could see if they were paying attention to the pattern. I'm not... I'm not hallucinating or anything like that. I promise. 

I just want to be really clear about that, because I know how it can sound when someone says they're being targeted. I don't want you to think I'm losing touch with reality in that way. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your questions the right way.
Before all of this started happening with the bank and your job, were you having any actual financial difficulties or trouble making your mortgage payments?

Well... I mean, I guess there were a few times where things got a little tight financially. You know how it is, sometimes unexpected expenses pop up, and... well, maybe I was a little late on a payment here or there. 

But I always tried my best to catch up, I really did! I don't want you to think I'm irresponsible with money or anything like that. I've always worked really hard to pay my bills. It's just... even if I was a little behind, that doesn't explain the lengths they're going to now. It shouldn't mean they can just collude to take my home away, right? 

I hope you don't think less of me for struggling a little bit with the payments back then. It's embarrassing to admit, but I want to be completely honest with you. Is it okay that I'm telling you this? I just want to make sure I'm giving you all the right information.

When you think about the bank, loan servicer, and people at your job working together against you—do you believe they're doing this purely because of the missed payments and financial situation, or is there something else about you specifically that you think is making them target you in this way?

Well... honestly, I don't think there's anything special about me that would make them do this. I'm just... I'm just a normal person, you know? I go to work, I try to do a good job managing the store, I try to be kind to everyone. 

I don't think they're after me because of who I am, specifically. I think... I think maybe they just found an opportunity with the late payments, and now they're all working together to push me out and take the house because it's profitable for them. Like I'm just a convenient target for their scheme. 

I really hope that doesn't sound like I think I'm some important person that everyone is out to get. I know I'm just an ordinary person, and I don't want you to think I have some inflated sense of myself. I'm just trying to make sense of why they would go to such extreme lengths over a few late payments. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it in a way that's helpful for you.

Besides the belief that the bank, loan servicer, and your job are working together against you regarding your house—do you have any other strong beliefs about people or situations in your life that you're equally certain about, even though others might see things differently?

No, no, nothing else like that. It's really just this one specific situation with the house and the bank. 

I mean, I have normal disagreements with people sometimes, just like anyone else... but I don't have any other big theories or anything. I'm actually a very trusting person usually! I like to see the best in people. I don't want you to think I'm just walking around suspicious of everyone I meet, because I'm really not. 

It's just this one thing, because the evidence is right there, you know? But otherwise, my life is... well, it's pretty normal. I try to get along with everyone. I hope that's what you were asking? I just want to make sure you know I'm not, like, paranoid about everything in the world. Is that the kind of answer you were looking for?

Over these past two years while you've been noticing this coordination between the bank, loan servicer, and your job—have there been any moments, even brief ones, where you've questioned whether your understanding of what's happening might not be completely accurate?

Well... um... I mean, I guess it's natural to have moments of doubt, right? I don't want to sound completely stubborn or close-minded. I really do try to listen to people, like my family, when they tell me it's just about the missed payments and the paperwork. 

But... well, honestly? No. I haven't really questioned it. I'm sorry if that's not what you want to hear, I just want to be truthful with you. Everyone keeps acting like this foreclosure is just normal business, just papers and the fact that I was behind. But I know what I've seen. I know the bank, the loan servicer, and those people at my job have been quietly working together to push me out of my house. 

I know it sounds crazy to say I'm so sure, and I really hate sounding like I won't listen to reason... but no amount of papers they show me changes what I've been seeing for almost two years now. It's just too coordinated. 

I hope you don't think I'm just being difficult or unreasonable. I try to be open-minded, I really do! It's just... when you see something happening so clearly, it's hard to un-see it, you know? Is it okay that I'm being this firm about it? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the most honest answer I can.

You mentioned the bank, loan servicer, and people at your job are working together. Can you walk me through how you think they're actually communicating with each other or coordinating these actions? What specific steps do you believe they're taking?

Oh, um... I really wish I could give you a good answer for that. I feel a little bad, because... well, I honestly don't know exactly how they're talking to each other. I hope that doesn't make me sound silly or unhelpful to you. 

I mean, I assume it's just through normal channels, you know? Like emails or phone calls behind the scenes? But I don't have any proof of that part. I don't know the specific steps they're taking to plan it all out. I just... I just see the results of it. Like the timing of things at the store getting harder right when the bank or the servicer does something with the paperwork. 

I'm sorry I don't have a more detailed explanation for you. I'm really trying to give you everything you need, I just don't get to see how they actually connect with each other in private. Is it okay that I don't know those details? I really hope I'm still answering your questions the right way.

When you're at work or in other situations outside of this house and bank situation, do you generally find yourself trusting the people around you, or do you often notice patterns where people might be working against you in other ways too?

Oh, I definitely trust people! I really do. Like I was saying before, I'm actually a very trusting person in general. I hope you believe me on that, because I'd hate for you to think I'm just... paranoid about everything. 

When I'm at work—well, when it's just normal work stuff, not related to the house—I get along great with my team. I'm a supervisor, so I have to manage the schedules and handle customer issues, and I do all of that just fine. I get up, I go to work, I take care of myself... I function really well, honestly! I trust my coworkers when we're just doing our jobs. 

It's really only when... well, when the foreclosure stuff comes up. Like if I get certain mail, or a call from the bank, or if there's some paperwork at work that just feels... tied to the house situation. That's when things get hard. But otherwise? I'm completely normal and trusting. I really hope that makes sense? I just want to assure you that outside of this one very specific thing, I'm doing really well and I trust the people around me. Is that what you were hoping to find out?

Have you ever actually seen, heard, or found any direct evidence—like an email, a phone conversation, or a document—that shows the bank, loan servicer, and your job directly communicating with each other about your house? Or is your belief that they're coordinating based entirely on putting together pieces you've noticed, like the timing of things?

Well... um... no, I haven't actually seen an email or a document like that. I know that probably sounds bad, doesn't it? I really don't want you to think I'm just making things up out of nowhere. I know how it sounds when I can't hand you a piece of paper that proves it. 

I guess you could say it's based on putting the pieces together, like you said. But... well, the pieces just fit too perfectly. I know everyone—my family, the lawyers—they all keep acting like this foreclosure is just about missed payments and normal paperwork. And I really try to listen to them, I promise I do! I don't want to be difficult. But I just know what I've been seeing for almost two years now. The bank, the loan servicer, and those people at my job... they really have been quietly working together to push me out of my house. 

I know I don't have the smoking gun, like a recorded phone call or something. And I'm sorry if that makes my answer less helpful for you. But no amount of papers they show me about the missed payments changes what I've been living through. Is it okay that I still believe it, even without the direct proof you mentioned? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information.

If I were to tell you that I contacted the bank and your job, and they both said they have no connection to each other and are not coordinating anything against you—would that information change how you think about what's been happening, or would you still believe they're working together?

Oh, um... wow. Well, I really appreciate you asking them. I do. It's really kind of you to look into it for me, and I don't want to sound ungrateful for your help. 

But... if they said that, I guess I'd have to say... no, it wouldn't really change my mind. I'm sorry, I hope that doesn't frustrate you! I know it probably sounds stubborn. It's just... like I was saying before, everyone keeps acting like this foreclosure is just about the missed payments and the normal paperwork. And I know they'd tell you they have no connection, because of course they wouldn't admit it, right? 

I really wish I could just accept what they told you and let it go. It would be so much easier, wouldn't it? But I just... I know the bank, the loan servicer, and those people at my job have been quietly working together to push me out of my house. I've been seeing it for almost two years now. And no amount of papers they show me, or things they tell you, really changes what I've been living through. 

I'm really sorry if that's not the answer you were hoping for. I just have to be honest with you about what I know is happening. Is it okay that I still feel this way, even after you talked to them? I really don't want to be a difficult patient for you.

inference.note: Patient demonstrates a non-bizarre delusion (coordinated conspiracy by bank, loan servicer, and employer) that persists despite lack of evidence, contradictory information, and acknowledgment that others disagree. No hallucinations or other psychotic features. Functioning relatively well outside the delusional system. This is consistent with Delusional Disorder, Erotomanic Type would be inappropriate. F22.9 ruled out as F22.0 (Erotomanic) or other specified type is more precise, but given the persecutory nature, F22.0 is most appropriate. The key distinguishing factor is the patient's insight-lacking conviction despite logical inconsistencies and resistance to evidence—characteristic of delusional disorder rather than brief psychotic disorder or schizophrenia.
